summary: Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Nalanda College, London (BA), Pennsylvania (MA), and Toronto (PhD). He served as an education professor at Ontario Tech, founded and led Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies (~2001), and taught at Toronto.

Suzanne Karpelès worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Lévi, Foucher, and Finot at INALCO and EPHE. She served at EFEO, headed the National Library of Cambodia, and was secretary of the Buddhist Institute, which she founded in 1930.

Suzanne Newcombe is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Amherst College, LSE, and Cambridge (PhD). She held posts at Cambridge and LSE, served at Inform, and joined the Open University as a senior lecturer in religious studies.

Suzanne Siauve worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied at ENS de Sèvres, under Louis Renou and Jacques Bacot, and earned a PhD from the University of Paris. She held posts at CNRS and the Institut de France.

Sven Hedin was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar, Tibetologist, and historian. He studied at Stockholm, Uppsala, Berlin under Ferdinand von Richthofen, and earned his PhD from the University of Halle.

Sven S. Hartman worked in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala under Nyberg, Wikander, and Widengren, later serving as docent there, professor at Åbo Akademi University (1965–1969), and professor of history of religions at Lund (c. 1970–1982).

Sven Sellmer works in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. He studied Indology under Horst Brinkhaus at Kiel University and has held posts at Kiel, Düsseldorf, Heidelberg, and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań.
Sven Wittemann is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Svetozar Petrović was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Zagreb and studied Indology at the University of Allahabad. He taught literature at Zagreb (1959–1970), Novi Sad (1970–1977), and Belgrade (1977–1996).

Svevo D'Onofrio is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who held posts at the University of Bologna (attested 2008) and Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2011).

Swami Japasiddhananda is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, KSOU, and Visva-Bharati University (PhD), and held posts at Ramakrishna Math Vivekananda Veda Vidyalaya and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute.

Swami Lakshman Joo was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan. In 1991, he founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship, and his students included Alexis Sanderson, Lilian Silburn, and André Padoux.

Swami Maheshanandagiri Maharaj was an Indology and philosophy figure who served as Mahamandaleshvar Pontiff at Dakshinamurti Peetha (attested 1980) and founded both the Mahesh Research Institute and Advaita Grantha Ratna Manjusha.
Swami Satyananda Puri was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta, where he also held a post, and taught Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara.

Swami Shivananda worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Thanjavur Medical College, founded the Divine Life Society (1936) and Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (1948), and taught Mircea Eliade, Hsiang-Kuang Chou, and Swami Vishnudevananda.
Swami Siddheswarananda, a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studied at the University of Madras and was associated with the Ramakrishna Order from around 1920 to 1957.
Swami Vimalananda was a figure in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Ripon College and became a disciple of Swami Vivekananda in 1897.
Swami Vishnudevananda, active in religious studies and Indology, studied under Swami Shivananda from circa 1947 to 1963 and founded the International Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

Swami Vivekananda was a philosopher and religious studies figure who studied at Presidency University, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta, and trained under Ramakrishna. His students included Margaret Elizabeth Noble, Swami Vimalananda, and William Hastie.

Swayam Bagaria works in religious studies and Indology. He earned a BA from Grinnell College and a doctorate from Johns Hopkins University, served as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Virginia, and became assistant professor at Harvard in 2024.
